result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_agg_degree_total()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get aggregate value from total degree of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26665-L26792){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_agg_degree_total( agg, conditions=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Aggregate total degree](/assets/graphs/get-agg-degree-total.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph with each node's total degree (in plus out) in a badge: A 3, B 3, C 4, D 3, E 1. The card sorts them as 1, 3, 3, 3, 4 and gives the median, 3.0." width="100%"} Computes a single aggregate statistic from the total degree values of all nodes. Works with both directed and undirected graphs. For directed graphs, total degree = indegree + outdegree. Each node's degree is found with `get_degree()` (parallel edges each count, a self-loop counts twice in undirected graphs, and edge weights are ignored), the nodes are optionally filtered with `conditions=`, and the remaining values are reduced to one number. Typical uses: - summarizing how connected a typical node is (`"mean"` or `"median"`) - finding the size of the largest hub (`"max"`) or checking for isolated nodes (`"min"` of `0`) - comparing the connectivity of node groups by running the same aggregation with different `conditions=` Without `conditions=`, `"mean"` gives the same value as `get_average_degree()`. All nodes in the graph are considered; any node selection is ignored. In directed graphs each degree is counted by scanning the edge list, so the cost grows with nodes times edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [agg]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Aggregation function to apply. Must be one of: - `"sum"`: Sum of all total degrees (twice the number of edges when no `conditions=` are given) - `"min"`: Minimum total degree - `"max"`: Maximum total degree - `"mean"`: Mean total degree - `"median"`: Median total degree (the mean of the two middle values when the number of nodes is even) [conditions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Filter function that takes a node object and returns `True` to include the node in the aggregation. If `None`, all nodes are included. The node object has `id`, `label`, and `attributes` properties; `attributes` is a dictionary, or `None` for a node without attributes, so a safe filter looks like `lambda n: (n.attributes or {}).get("kind") == "gene"`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The computed aggregate total degree value. Returns `0.0` if no nodes match the conditions. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `agg=` is not a valid aggregation function. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_agg_degree_in`) : The same summary for in-degree (directed graphs only). [](`~get_agg_degree_out`) : The same summary for out-degree (directed graphs only). [](`~get_average_degree`) : The mean degree over all nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a random directed graph with 20 nodes and 35 edges, each edge adds one to the degree of both of its endpoints, so the mean total degree is `2 * 35 / 20`, or `3.5`: ::: {#0d68d58f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_gnm_graph(20, 35, seed=23) graph.get_agg_degree_total('mean') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3.5 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#109db189 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_agg_degree_total('median') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3.0 ``` ::: ::: Unlike `get_agg_degree_in()`/`get_agg_degree_out()`, this also works on undirected graphs -- every node in a cycle has degree `2`, so the mean is exactly `2.0`: ::: {#1a522df9 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph_undirected = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph_undirected.add_cycle_graph(10) graph_undirected.get_agg_degree_total('mean') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2.0 ``` ::: ::: With `conditions=`, the hub of a star (node `1`, with degree `5`) can be left out, which shows that every other node has degree `1`: ::: {#9583383e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(6) star.get_agg_degree_total('max', conditions=lambda n: n.id != 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: :::
